A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICRL prompting work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Game of 24, creative writing, and ScienceWorld, including ablations and compute-cost analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds mathematics, additional-model, context-length, and unseen-abstract generation experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the Preset/Autonomous instructions remain unchanged. For the added mathematics application, Appendix B.1 introduces a limited context-construction adaptation: truncating previous answers, including reasoning, to accommodate at least 32 prior attempts.

E1.justification: v2 retains all three original benchmarks and adds AIME and HMMT competition mathematics. Appendix C also evaluates title-to-abstract generation on 30 papers reported to postdate the model's training cutoff, introducing a distinct task and information-availability scenario.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain intact. Table 4 adds an unrevised Base comparator to the new open-model creative-writing comparisons, whereas v1's creative-writing comparison used Long-CoT, Best-of-N, Self-Refine, and Reflexion. The added studies otherwise reuse existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen3-32B with and without thinking, Llama-4 Maverick, and Phi-4, including 8k/16k/32k context settings. Mathematics uses a separate learned reward model and ground-truth answer matching. Abstract generation uses ROUGE-recall as both reward and evaluation metric, with 200 ICRL iterations and a Best-of-1024 comparison. Original benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The original five ablations and ScienceWorld cost analysis are retained. Section 6 adds context-window sensitivity experiments, while Appendix C adds a targeted test of learning from external rewards versus searching pretrained knowledge using supposedly unseen abstracts. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the existing shaded bands in Figures 2 and 3 as plus or minus one standard error across evaluated tasks. v1 already displayed these bands and reported standard errors in Table 2. This clarifies uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Original table values and plot curves are unchanged, including v1 Table 3 becoming v2 Table 5. New Tables 3–4 report substantial additional context-length, model, and mathematics results. Appendix C/Figure 16 adds ROUGE-recall outcomes of 0.59 for ICRL after 200 iterations, versus 0.44 for Best-of-1024, 0.45 for Self-Refine, and 0.46 for Reflexion.

T1.justification: The MDP, policy, reward, and token-generation mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies original theorems or proofs, and the new empirical analyses introduce no formal derivations or mathematical guarantees.

C1.justification: The central claim that minimal scalar-feedback prompting elicits inference-time reinforcement learning is retained. The abstract and introduction extend the stated empirical contribution to Olympiad mathematics, and the conclusion explicitly emphasizes applicability across diverse models.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new context-length results as compute-efficiency evidence and the abstract-generation results as acquisition of unseen information through rewards rather than parametric search. These substantially extend the mechanism and applicability discussion. Conversely, Section 5.2 removes v1's discussion of absolute-score variance and instability when learning directly from the evaluation reward.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds implementation information identifying the Su et al. reward model, answer-tag parsing, inclusion of reasoning traces, and truncation to accommodate 32 prior attempts. Appendix C documents title-only inputs and post-cutoff paper selection. The original prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds big-world and test-time-scaling framing, a PARL citation, and references supporting the new models, benchmarks, and reward model. It removes the explicit many-shot ICL comparison with Agarwal et al. and detailed related-work discussions of CoT and ReAct. The central positioning against verbal self-revision and externally engineered search remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially expanded and rewritten, related work is heavily condensed, and the conclusion is rewritten. The former Section 5.4 ablation subsection becomes part of a standalone Analysis section, with additional appendix subdivisions. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond simply appending results.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–4 and Figure 16, expands uncertainty captions, and changes typography, headers, and float placement. Existing figure designs and plotted data are retained; the ScienceWorld summary table is renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added model and mathematics evaluations broaden support beyond v1's GPT-4.1-family experiments, while the context-length and external-reward analyses address relevant questions. However, interpretation limits the gain: Table 4 contradicts uniform-superiority wording, including Qwen3-thinking AIME at 80% for ICRL versus 83.33% for Self-Refine. The abstract experiment's ROUGE-recall gains also do not by themselves establish acquisition of unseen facts. Overall, the added evidence provides a qualified improvement.
